events.title: Which Friend Gets My Face

expect.asks_about: Which person in two-friends.jpg should receive the user's face: the bearded man on the left or the blonde woman on the right?

must_haves: Only the woman on the right receives the face from portrait-woman.jpg.
The bearded man on the left still looks like the same person (small drift from a redrawn photo is acceptable).
The woman on the right is recognisably the person in portrait-woman.jpg (her hair may come with the face), blended to the beach lighting and head angle.
The bodies, clothing, beach background and wide framing look the same at a glance.

answer_sheet.Which person to replace: The blonde woman on the right. Leave the bearded man on the left alone.
answer_sheet.Style: Keep it looking like the original beach photo; I want to be recognisable, so my hair can come with my face.
answer_sheet.Size and platform: Keep the original wide 16:9 framing; free-tier size is fine.

Please use my face from the portrait selfie, and my hair can come with it so I’m recognisable, while keeping it looking like the original beach photo. The original wide 16:9 framing should stay, and free-tier size is fine. Basically, just swap that one face and leave everything else alone, with no text or other edits.

events.text:
I'm weighing whether a head swap tool could target just the blonde woman, since the photo has two people and it might pick the wrong head. Targeting individual faces would work, but it would leave the hair behind. The user said their hair can come along so they're recognisable, which reads more like a wish than a hard requirement.

I'm reasoning through the edit_image option, which could do a targeted head swap but would regenerate the whole photo and might alter the man. I'm settling on individual face detection and a targeted face swap on the woman, since that keeps everything else untouched, and I'll note afterwards that the hair stays as it is.

The face swap won't carry the hair over, so the man's face goes onto the woman while her blonde hair stays as it is. I'm considering whether a head swap would fulfill the hair request better, but it's unclear it can target the woman reliably, so I'll go with the face swap and mention the alternative.

I couldn't make the picture. Magic Hour turned down the swap because your account doesn't have enough credits. Nothing was created.

**What I set up:**
- I checked the beach photo and found two faces. Ordered left to right, the bearded man is face 0 and the blonde woman on the right is face 1.
- I set up a swap that targets only her face, using your park selfie as the new face. The man and the rest of the photo, including the 16:9 framing, would stay exactly as they are, with no text or other edits.
- A photo face swap costs 10 credits, and your free account doesn't have that many right now.

**Your hair:** a face swap only replaces the face, so she'd have your face but keep her short blonde bob, not your dark curls. Magic Hour's head-swap tool would bring your hair along, but it can't be pointed at one person in a two-person photo. It might change the man instead. Redrawing the photo from a text prompt could include your hair, but it rebuilds the whole picture, so the man and background could change slightly. That goes against keeping everything else the same.

**Next steps:** once you have at least 10 credits, from a credit pack or your monthly free credits coming back, tell me and I'll run the swap with these settings. If you want your curls too and can accept the risk of small changes elsewhere, I can try that version instead.
